name: Andres LeCompte, Councilor and Lord of Banu Duval

system.concept: Diablerist Concealing a Terrifying Inherited Secret
system.title: Councilor; Lord of Banu Duval
system.biography:
Background

Embraced in 1801 by his lover Jean-Baptiste Duval, founder of Banu Duval, at his own tearful insistence, Andres LeCompte spent over a century watching his sire grow distant, spending ever more time and wealth on other French @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} migres while claiming it was all done for their love. When Duval accepted a seat on the Consultative Council in the 1920s, Andres's resentment finally boiled over. Amid the chaos of Black Saturday, he crept into his sire's haven in Bulaq and diablerized him, seizing his position and title with surprising ease.

Since then, Andres has begun to unravel. He struggles to control the vitae now coursing through him, suffers vivid, alien dreams, and repeatedly loses time, once waking mid-search through his own diablerized sire's papers concerning a group called the Ennead. He has come to suspect, with mounting dread, that Duval was never truly his sire in any simple sense — that Duval may have engineered his own khitta and even Napoleon's withdrawal from Egypt centuries ago — and that whatever LeCompte diablerized was far older and more dangerous than a mere @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elder.

Roleplaying Hints

Present unshakeable elegance and social command in public. Privately, let flickers of genuine confusion and dread break through — you are no longer entirely certain what you did to yourself the night you killed your sire.
system.notes: Diablerized his sire, Jean-Baptiste Duval, during Black Saturday and inherited memory-fragments suggesting Duval was connected to a mysterious group called the Ennead and was far older/more significant than believed. Suspects his own vassal Fahd al-Zawba'a (the Whirlwind) knows more about him than he lets on, and separately believes there is a dormant, dangerous power within the elder @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Muhandis that must be stopped before it awakens.

system.description: You may double the range of your sight and hearing and sharpen your other senses to remarkable acuity, perceiving things ordinary folk cannot. A sudden sensory assault, such as a loud noise or strong odor, numbs the affected sense for the rest of the scene and stuns you for a turn unless you spend a Willpower Trait. You may also receive uncontrollable visions of past or future events.

Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.
By spending a Blood Trait, you gain one additional action at the end of the turn, after all basic actions resolve.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By spending a Blood Trait, you gain a further additional action at the end of the turn, on top of any gained from Swiftness.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By hissing and baring your vampiric features in a Social Challenge, you strike terror into a victim who, if defeated, flees and avoids you for the rest of the scene or hour, risking an extra Trait to act against you if cornered.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

items.name: Presence — 2 Intermediate — Command the Wary Steed

system.description:
Through use of this power the Cainite can cause enemies' mounts to rear and bolt, singly or en masse, by the strength of his gaze alone, or bolster the courage and tractability of allied steeds for greater control in battle.

System: The player spends a Willpower point and rolls Manipulation + Animal Ken (difficulty 7). Enemy mounts become terrified and nigh uncontrollable: Ride roll difficulties increase by three and mounted combat becomes impossible. Friendly mounts become far more pliant (-2 difficulty on all Ride rolls) and may be coerced into situations they would normally avoid.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Three: Zealots

system.description:
Named for the legendary (and supposedly fae) progenitor of the houses of Anjou and Lusignan, this power lets a Toreador sway others through song. If the Artisan can phrase her request in the form of a song, her words take on the weight of a nigh-irresistible command.

System: The player states the suggestion she wishes to weave into the song and describes the song's nature. Everyone within earshot must resist or unknowingly submit to the request. The effect lasts as long as the Toreador continues singing or until the target leaves her presence; commands requiring the victim to leave the singer's presence can be resisted once more after the enchanting voice fades. Listeners outside the Toreador's immediate presence may notice something odd about the performance, though it registers as little more than an exceptionally fine one; other Toreador within earshot are immediately entranced. As a side benefit, knowledge of this power makes the character a superlative singer even when the power itself is not invoked.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)
system.duration: As long as the Toreador continues singing, or until the target leaves her presence

vtmlarp.source: Cairo by Night, Chapter Four: Dead Among the Dead
